question: Should OpenClaw accept RFC 0018’s opt-in `gateway.readiness` contract, including required/advisory aggregation, subject identity, and activation-scoped plugin readiness providers, as the intended public API boundary?
rationale: This is a new configuration and plugin extension contract whose stable shape, upgrade behavior, and ownership cannot be selected safely from source review alone.

options.title: Accept the proposed v1 boundary
options.body: Approve the opt-in contract and use the RFC as the implementation and compatibility reference for the linked readiness work.

options.title: Narrow before acceptance
options.body: Retain core canonical readiness only and defer subject identity or plugin-provider registration until their API ownership is separately agreed.

options.title: Decline the direction
options.body: Keep the existing Gateway readiness evaluator and avoid adding this configuration and plugin API surface for now.

recommendation.title: Accept the proposed v1 boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the opt-in contract and use the RFC as the implementation and compatibility reference for the linked readiness work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available adjacent RFC and readiness-stack contributor who can clarify tradeoffs, while the final product decision remains with repository maintainers.
